recommendations.regimenLabel: Acute attack — NSAID, colchicine or corticosteroid (choose by comorbidity)
steps: Aspirate the joint — crystals confirm gout/pseudogout; Gram stain/culture EXCLUDES septic arthritis.
Acute attack: NSAID, or colchicine, or corticosteroid (oral/intra-articular) — choose by comorbidity.
Rest, ice, analgesia; continue any established urate-lowering therapy through the attack.
Do NOT start/stop allopurinol during an acute flare for the first time; initiate urate-lowering later with prophylaxis.
Address risk factors (diuretics, alcohol, renal function).

drugRefs.freq: twice daily until attack settles, then taper
drugRefs.why: First-line for acute flare in patients without renal/GI/cardiovascular contraindication; co-prescribe gastroprotection if indicated.

drugRefs.dose: 0.5 mg (500 mcg) 2–3 times daily (e.g. 1 mg then 0.5 mg 1 h later on day 1)
drugRefs.why: Useful when NSAIDs are contraindicated. Reduce dose in renal impairment and with interacting drugs; low-dose regimens are as effective and better tolerated.

drugRefs.freq: for ~5 days (or intra-articular for a single joint)
drugRefs.why: Preferred where NSAIDs and colchicine are contraindicated (e.g. renal impairment); intra-articular steroid for an isolated large joint once sepsis excluded.

refs: Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 22e — Gout and Other Crystal-Associated Arthropathies
ACR Guideline for the Management of Gout
EULAR Recommendations for the Management of Gout

recommendations.regimenLabel: Urate-lowering therapy (after the flare, with prophylaxis)

drugRefs.dose: start 100 mg once daily (50 mg if CKD), titrate to serum urate target <360 micromol/L
drugRefs.why: Long-term urate-lowering to prevent recurrence. Do not start during an acute flare for the first time; when starting, cover with flare prophylaxis (low-dose colchicine or NSAID).

refs: Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 22e — Gout and Other Crystal-Associated Arthropathies
ACR Guideline for the Management of Gout

decision.label: Confirm crystals; exclude septic arthritis; treat flare

confirm: Acute monoarthritis (often 1st MTP/knee) — confirm with joint aspiration showing crystals; ALWAYS exclude septic arthritis.
disposition: Outpatient; admit if septic arthritis not excluded.
